title: Genesis: scheduling a working band without anyone chasing
audience: Anyone who coordinates a group (a team, volunteers, members) and loses hours finding dates and chasing replies.

intent.primary: How can a group find a date everyone can make without someone chasing replies by hand?
related: How does an automatic chasing system decide who to nudge?

uniqueValue: A tool in daily use that finds a date, chases only the people who haven't replied, and confirms. The public demo lets a visitor try it with a pretend band.

seo.title: Genesis scheduling and chasing case study | Chris Demetriou
seo.description: How Genesis finds a date a whole band can make, chases only the people who haven't replied, and confirms, with no one doing it by hand.

claims.text: Genesis finds a date everyone can make, chases anyone who hasn't replied, and confirms.
Genesis is running a real band.

sources.ref: Decision Log, 18 Oct 2026 (Genesis is described as a live app)

claims.text: A public demo uses fictional data and a pretend band.

body.text: Genesis does it automatically: it finds a date everyone can make, chases only the people who haven't replied, and confirms once everyone is in. It is running a real band.

body.heading: Try it
body.text: The public demo uses fictional data and a pretend band, so you can see the whole flow without signing up.
